title: Treasury estimates the 2026 changes would raise rents by less than $2 a week for a household on the median rent
oneLiner: The official estimate of the rent effect is small.
body: Treasury's budget modelling puts the rent effect of restricting negative gearing and reworking the capital gains discount at under $2 a week at the median, and estimates about 35,000 fewer homes over a decade, more than offset in its view by the budget's supply measures. Its secretary told the Senate the measures mainly shift ownership from investors to owner-occupiers.
contextBackground: Treasury's number is the government's answer to the rent objection. It is an estimate of a policy not yet in force, so it is a fact about the modelling rather than about rents.
contextDisagreement: The industry's modellers say Treasury understates investor withdrawal; Treasury says the industry's model assumes investors leave and nobody buys the homes they sell.

evidenceItems.citation: The Nightly, 29 May 2026 — Treasury figures and secretary Jenny Wilkinson's evidence

otherClaim.title: Limiting negative gearing to new builds would make housing materially more affordable

claimItself.title: Limiting negative gearing to new builds would make housing materially more affordable
claimItself.oneLiner: Removing the tax advantage for investors in existing homes would take heat out of the market first-home buyers compete in.
claimItself.body: Investors and first-home buyers bid for the same established dwellings. Removing a concession available only to one side would, proponents argue, shift enough demand to make a visible difference to prices and to who wins at auction.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Grattan Institute modelling found that limiting negative gearing and halving the capital gains discount would lower house prices by about 2 per cent

otherClaim.title: Winding back negative gearing would push rents up as investors leave the market

claimItself.title: Winding back negative gearing would push rents up as investors leave the market
claimItself.oneLiner: Fewer landlords means fewer rentals, and fewer rentals means higher rents.
claimItself.body: If the after-tax return on rental property falls, some investors will sell and fewer will buy. Opponents of reform argue that the resulting withdrawal of rental stock would raise rents for the tenants the policy is meant to help.

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: Modelling commissioned by the property industry forecasts rents about $9 a week higher and roughly 8,700 fewer homes by 2030 under the changes
